_doc: BASELINE of pre-existing DEAD/WEAK schema. DEBT REGISTER, not approval. NEW dead schema fails the build. Wire an object and DELETE its entry (the guard prints entries that became wired so the register drains).
_scope: SCHEMA REACHABILITY IN CODE only. This guard cannot prove rows are populated, that a poster runs, or that reverse drill-through exists in the UI. Those are live-data audits (LAW 0: prod wins). Never cite this guard as proof the books are wired.

_verdicts.none: identifier appears NOWHERE in non-test source — storage with no reader at all
_verdicts.weak: identifier appears in the codebase but in NO file that touches this table — the substring illusion (e.g. mdata.drivers.employment_status, superseded by driver_employment_status_id in 0343)

_recapture: 2026-07-21 — coverage went from 1,074 ADD COLUMN-only objects to 5,740 live columns (inline CREATE TABLE columns were 81% of the schema and were invisible), and whole-corpus substring matching was replaced by whole-token, table-context matching. The count grew because the guard now sees what it always claimed to check. DO-block DDL (real CREATE TABLE inside $$ bodies) and comma-separated inline columns are now parsed too — the prior revision discarded dollar-quoted bodies entirely.

outbox.outbox_queue is a RETIRED duplicate of outbox.events. Verified on prod 2026-08-03 (positive control mdata.vendors=2,828): 49 rows, ALL 'PENDING', attempts=0 on every row, oldest 2026-06-16 — nothing has ever drained it, because processor.ts reads outbox.events (31,622 rows, 31,618 delivered). This column became reader-less in the SAME PR that repointed 9 of its 11 producers onto the live table; its siblings available_at/locked_at/processed_at were already baselined here for the same reason and are the pre-existing evidence of it. Retiring the table is a MIGRATION and therefore owner-gated, so it is tracked separately rather than smuggled in — the two remaining writers are a deprecated unreachable route file and the QBO write-back pair that stays off by owner ruling.

DEAD-SCHEMA-OUTBOX-QUEUE-EXTERNAL-ID-UNREAD (CC-3 2026-08-27): outbox.queue has an INSERT-only caller (lists-hub.routes.ts force-qbo-sync) and genuinely NO SELECT/UPDATE anywhere in apps/backend/src — confirmed via repo-wide grep, zero hits. The table has no dequeue/processor at all, so external_id (meant to record the remote system's assigned id after a successful push) is unread because nothing processes a row past insert, not because of a missing read on this one column specifically. The migration's own header comment says this exact thing: "Long-term outbox unification with accounting.outbox_events is tracked separately" — building a real QBO-sync processor is a genuine new feature (and QBO write-back-sensitive), not a drive-by reader. Baselined rather than fabricating a consumer.
